subject: Rio Grande Plan
comment: Dear Members of the Salt Lake City Council, I am writing to express my strong support for the Rio Grande Plan and to encourage you to choose this visionary project as a critical step in the ongoing revitalization of our city. The Rio Grande neighborhood holds a significant place in Salt Lake City's history, and it is essential that we invest in its future by addressing the challenges it currently faces. The comprehensive approach outlined in the Rio Grande Plan, with its focus on homelessness, public safety, urban redevelopment, and community engagement, reflects the values and priorities of our city. By adopting this plan, we have the opportunity to transform the Rio Grande area into a vibrant, safe, and inclusive neighborhood that honors its historical significance while meeting the needs of today's residents and businesses. Addressing homelessness in our community is of paramount importance. The plan's commitment to relocating and improving homeless services, along with the provision of permanent supportive housing, offers a compassionate and effective solution. By providing individuals experiencing homelessness with the resources they need to regain stability, we can create a more equitable and humane city. Moreover, enhancing public safety in the Rio Grande area is crucial for fostering a sense of security and well-being among all who live, work, and visit the neighborhood. The plan's strategies for increasing law enforcement presence and improving public safety measures will help reduce crime and create a welcoming environment for everyone. The proposed urban redevelopment initiatives, which include restoring historic buildings and promoting mixed-use developments, will breathe new life into the Rio Grande neighborhood. These efforts will not only preserve the area's cultural heritage but also attract new businesses and residents, contributing to the overall economic vitality of Salt Lake City. Lastly, I commend the emphasis on community engagement in the Rio Grande Plan. Ensuring that the voices of local residents, businesses, and organizations are heard and considered is essential for the success of any redevelopment effort. I am confident that, with continued collaboration and dialogue, the Rio Grande Plan will reflect the diverse needs and aspirations of our community. In conclusion, I urge you to endorse the Rio Grande Plan and take the necessary steps to implement this comprehensive and forward-thinking project. By doing so, we can create a brighter future for the Rio Grande neighborhood and for Salt Lake City as a whole. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely, Kaitlyn Gatchel Herriman

subject: Support for CIP Public Infrastructure Improvements on Fayette Avenue
comment: Dear Dan Dugan, The Central Ninth Community Council is requesting your support for the CIP public infrastructure improvements project on Fayette Avenue. This initiative, spanning from Washington Street to 200 West, represents a significant step forward in enhancing the quality of life for our community. The proposed project is poised to address several key aspects that are crucial for fostering a vibrant, walkable, and safe neighborhood. By completing street and parking paving on the south side of Fayette Avenue, installing a sidewalk, curb, and gutter on the north side, and lighting on both sides, the project will significantly enhance pedestrian accessibility and safety. The planned enhancements—including the paving of a parking area, installation of street trees, landscaping, and street lighting—will not only beautify the area but also contribute to the overall functionality and appeal of the neighborhood. This project is especially noteworthy in light of its proximity to the 900 South TRAX stop, which underscores the importance of walkability in supporting public transit usage and reducing reliance on personal vehicles. The integration of these improvements aligns with the zoning goals for the area (FBUN-2) and the broader vision of creating a walkable community. This project will be a significant asset to our community, addressing critical issues related to walkability, open space, and parking. The synergy between the proposed city-funded improvements and UDOT and UTA initiatives will foster a more cohesive and inviting environment for residents and visitors alike. I strongly urge the City Council to support and approve the funding for this project. Your support will be instrumental in realizing these much-needed improvements and in contributing to the ongoing revitalization of our community. Thank you for your attention to this important matter. Should you require any additional information or wish to discuss this project further, please do not hesitate to contact me. Sincerely, Douglas Flagler Central Ninth Community Council Chair

subject: Memory Grove & City Creek Parks Improvement Grant
comment: Dear Members of the Salt Lake City Council, On behalf of Preservation Utah, I am writing to express our strong support for the proposed improvements to Memory Grove and City Creek Parks, as included in the Mayor's 2025 budget. For the past 30 years, we have had the privilege of operating Memorial House within Memory Grove Park, and we have witnessed firsthand the importance of these parks as historical and cultural landmarks in our community. Memory Grove and City Creek Parks are beautiful green spaces that serve as living memorials to our community's history. They are places where citizens and visitors alike can reflect on the past while enjoying Salt Lake City's natural beauty. However, the passage of time has led to significant wear and tear on the parks' infrastructure, and many of the monuments and pathways now need urgent repair. The proposed improvements are essential for preserving the integrity and safety of these beloved parks. Replacing the deteriorating street lamp poles, refurbishing the historic monuments, and enhancing pedestrian safety on the switchbacks are crucial to ensure they remain safe, welcoming, and historically accurate for all who visit. We also strongly support the development of a Preservation & Maintenance Plan for Memory Grove Park and the Freedom Trail. This plan will provide a roadmap for the long-term care of these parks, ensuring that they continue to serve as vital parts of our community. Thank you for considering this important matter. Sincerely, Brandy Strand Executive Director preservationutah.org

subject: CIP Budget Comments: #451562: Pedestrian Safety / HAWK at Richmond St. and Zenith Ave.
comment: Dear City Council Members, I've been a District 7 resident for 3 years, living at REDACTED with my family. I'm sharing budget comments about CIP application #451562: Pedestrian Safety / HAWK at Richmond St. and Zenith Ave. The Richmond/Zenith intersection is in the growing Brickyard area and is part of the 1300 E Reconstruction Project. My neighbors and I walk kids to daycare, use the 213 bus stops, and travel to Nibley Park School through the Zenith/Richmond intersection. Although there is considerable pedestrian traffic that will only continue to grow, this 5-lane intersection remains inadequately equipped to protect those walking, biking, and using transit. I've been involved in, and have witnessed, countless near-misses with cars hitting pedestrians. Just this morning, cars were trying to pass other cars that stopped while my husband and toddler were walking in the crosswalk. Drivers speed between the controlled intersections at Highland and Brickyard, and do not see or ignore the flashing yellow lights and pedestrians at the Richmond/Zenith crosswalk. Neighbors who signed the CIP petition described this intersection as "scary," a "nightmare," and "dangerous." Although there are benefits to including a HAWK installation as part of the 1300 E project, my understanding is this CIP application has so far been denied due to its estimated cost of $500,000. I've heard from our councilperson that this cost could be split: $50,000 to design the project this year and then $450,000 for construction next year. My family and I support this compromise with the addition of lower-cost, interim pedestrian protections. Crosswalk paint, pedestrian flags, and state law signs in the crosswalk are some ideas for lower-cost safety improvements to this intersection. Anything the city can install while we wait for a HAWK signal will improve pedestrian safety. Thank you for your time and I hope to receive your support for funding $50,000 to design this project and install lower-cost pedestrian safety measures this coming year. Sincerely, Laura Kendellen
